utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is Case Number IT-02-64-I, the Prosecutor versus Ljubomir Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, madam, and good afternoon to you. Mr. Borovcanin, before we proceed any further, I would like to make sure that the proceedings and every part of the proceedings, which are being conducted in English, are being translated to you in your own language or in a language which you can understand.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I understand the translation I'm receiving. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Please, if at any time during the proceedings there are problems with interpretation, do draw my attention straight away because it's important that you are in a position to follow what is happening here at any given time. Okay. You may sit down for the time being. Let's have the appearances. For the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Peter McCloskey, and with me Janet Stewart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, and good afternoon to you and your team. Appearances for the accused Mr. Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROHAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Colleen Rohan for Mr. Borovcanin. I'm appearing as duty counsel today. And also with me is Mr. Miodrag Stojanovic. He is an attorney who has a prior relationship with Mr. Borovcanin and I would request, with the Court's permission, that he could be present during the proceedings for this initial appearance. Also present with us is Dragoslav Djukic, who is an interpreter for Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I thank you, Madam Rohan. As you know, I've made an exception to the rule allowing the gentleman, Mr. Miodrag Stojanovic, and his interpreter to be present by your side. The understanding is, of course, that they have no right of a presentation today. That is why I insisted that they do not wear robes and that it's important that they make no intervention until Mr. Stojanovic's position is regularised.

utterances.speaker: MS. ROHAN
utterances.text: I appreciate that very much. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you. Now, Mr. Borovcanin, something to which I give fundamental importance: We will be proceeding with what is known as initial appearance, your initial appearance in this case. It is my duty, my responsibility, to inform you that before this Tribunal you enjoy a right to remain silent throughout the entire proceedings, not just today but in all other hearings that you will be summoned to attend to. Basically, what this means is that no one can force you to answer any question that is put to you or to make any declaration before or to this Tribunal or to anyone else for that matter. I will be in the course of today's initial hearing be making -- putting some questions to you, obviously, which fall under this category as well. And -- but what is important is that I want to make sure that you are aware of this right that you enjoy throughout the entire process here.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. If you have any questions in regard, please do not hesitate to put them through your duty counsel for today. You may sit down. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. For the moment I have no questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down. I take it that later on there will be or there is going to be a waiver as regards the reading of the indictment. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. ROHAN
utterances.text: You are correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I will limit myself to give some information, not only for the sake of your client but also and primarily so for the sake of those who are following these proceedings. I think in accomplishing or seeking to accomplish our role, this Tribunal has a duty to keep the public informed of what the indictment basically consists of. The accused Mr. Borovcanin is included with the indictment case number IT-02-64, which was confirmed on the 6th of September, 2002 -- actually, it was signed on the 6th of September, 2002, and was confirmed by my colleague Judge Wolfgang Schomburg. Initially it was under seal, but then it was made public by an order of this Tribunal on the 27th of September of the same year, of 2002. The indictment is pretty much detailed, and I will not of course go into each and every detail that is contained therein, but I will give the basics. The indictment alleges that you, Mr. Ljubomir Borovcanin, while you were deputy commander of the special police brigade, which throughout the indictment is referred to as the SPB, of the MUP, which is the Ministry of Interior, that you were present in and around the areas of Bratunac, Potocari, Sandici, Kravica, Srebrenica, and Zvornik from the 11th of July to the 18th of July of 1995. According to the indictment, you were ordered to report to Radislav Krstic, who was then Chief of Staff of the Drina Corps of the VRS, which is the Bosnian Serb army. The indictment also alleges that units under your command were deployed in and around the areas of Potocari, Sandici, Kravica, and Zvornik from the 12th of July to the 18th of July of 1995. In the several days following the attack on Srebrenica, according to the Prosecutor, VRS and MUP forces captured, detained, summarily executed, and buried over 7.000 Bosnian Muslim men and boys from the Srebrenica enclave, and in addition forcibly transferred the Bosnian Muslim women and children of Srebrenica out of the enclave. The indictment which was confirmed against you, Mr. Borovcanin, refers to your alleged involvement in the opportunistic killings in Potocari, opportunistic killings in Bratunac, wide-scale and organised killings in Potocari and Tisca, killings and mistreatment of prisoners captured along the Bratunac-Milici road, and wide-scale and organised killings in the Zvornik area as well as other opportunistic killings. I will dwell on this for a while. With regard to the opportunistic killings in Potocari, there are instances which refer to the 12th and the 13th of July of 1995, referring to killings of several Bosnian Muslim men and women. With regard to the opportunistic killings in Bratunac, again the events that the indictment refers to relate to the 12th of July on one occasion where more than 50 Bosnian Muslim men were taken from a hangar behind the Vuk Karadzic elementary school in Bratunac and summarily executed, and other events which allegedly took place on the 13th of July and also on one occasion on the -- in the morning of the 15th of July, where again several persons were summarily executed. With regard to wide-scale and organised killings in Potocari and Tisca, the indictment refers to events that took place on the 12th of July, 1995 in Potocari in between the zinc factory and Alija's house, where 80 to 100 Muslim -- Bosnian Muslim men were executed by decapitation. And as far as Tisca is concerned on the 13th of July, again we have a number of men and women who were summarily executed. With regard to the killings and mistreatment of prisoners captured along the Bratunac-Milici road, there are several events, and these relate to those events that took place in the Jadar River on the 13th of July, Cerska Valley, also on the 13th of July. Kravica warehouse, again on the 13th of July, but then also on the 14th and 16th of July. Sandici meadow. Again we're talking about the 13th and 14th of July, all of 1995. Kravica market, again, it's on the 13th and 14th of July. Kravica school, 13th and 14th of July. Bratunac-Milici road after the 13th of July through about the 16th of July. With regard to the Zvornik area, the indictment alleges killings which took place in Orahovac near Lazete, on the 13th of July. The Petkovci school on the 14th of July. The dam here Petkovci on the 14th and 15th of July. Pilica school on the 14th and 15th of July, Branjevo Military Farm on the 16th of July. Pilica cultural centre on the 16th of July. Kozluk on the 16th of July, and in most instances the Prosecution alleges that on the following day then members of the Zvornik Engineering Company of the Zvornik Brigade and others buried the victims or disposed of the bodies. There are several other opportunistic killings that are mentioned in the indictment, and according to the Prosecution these happened, as far as the Bratunac Brigade zone is concerned, in Nova Kasaba, Konjevic Polje, Glogova. And then there are allegations directed specifically to the Bratunac Brigade in relation to -- and certain identifying individuals that were, according to the indictment, executed. As regards the Zvornik Brigade, there are similar allegations, and the events are supposed to have taken place in Nezuk in particular, and in other areas nearby. The Prosecution alleges also that you, Mr. Borovcanin, together with other VRS and MUP officers and units who are identified in the indictment and which I don't need to repeat here, you were a member of and knowingly participated in a joint criminal enterprise, the common purpose of which was, amongst other things, to forcibly transfer the women and children from the Srebrenica enclave to Kladanj on the 12th and 13th of July, 1995, and to capture, detain, summarily execute by firing squad, bury and re-bury thousands of Bosnian Muslim boys aged 16 to 60 from the Srebrenica enclave from the 12th of July, 1995 until and about the 19th of July 1995. The indictment - and this is very important for you to understand - charges you under two different modes of criminal liability. You're charged under Article 7(1) of the Statute, which is individual criminal responsibility, but also Article 7(3) of our Statute, which holds responsible for crimes mentioned in the Statute itself those who are criminally responsible in virtue of their superior command. We refer to this as superior criminal responsibility. This permeates the entire indictment. This is how it starts and this is how it ends. You have got several counts in this indictment, and I will start with the first one, which is perhaps the most serious of them all, and this is one count of complicity in genocide, genocide being one of the crimes that our Statute contemplates. I will come to the counts later on today, or if you're not going to enter a plea today, in due course when we have the additional initial appearance. Then you have four counts of crimes against humanity. Again, crimes against humanity are crimes contemplated by our Statute in Article 5. And namely, these four crimes that are being brought forward against you are extermination; murder; persecution on political, racial, and religious grounds; and inhuman acts consisting of forcible transfer. Then finally you have one count of the laws or customs of war which is contemplated under Article 3 of the Statute, and the violations, according to the Prosecution, according to the indictment, consists in murder. That's the information I have as regards the indictment. I want you to know, Mr. Borovcanin, that by order of the President of this Tribunal, His Excellency Professor Theodore Meron, dated 1st April of this year, your case was assigned to my Trial Chamber, that is Trial Chamber II, of which I am the Presiding Judge. As such, my capacity as Presiding Judge on the same day, that is 1st April of this year, I appointed myself, I designated myself for the purpose -- to be the Pre-Trial Judge for the purpose of today's initial appearance. Who will deal with the pre-trial proceedings, I have still not decided, but eventually I will take the decision in the next few days and you will be informed accordingly. And that applies also if today's initial appearance is adjourned to the additional initial appearance. It may not necessarily be myself. I am now going to proceed with the so-called procedural part of the initial appearance, and this I am doing pursuant to Rule 62 of our Rules of Procedure and Evidence. And I suggest to you, Mr. Borovcanin, that if you have not yet been given a copy of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of this Tribunal, that you try and acquire one. They exist in your own language, and they will be useful to have by your side all the time. After having finished with the initial part of the initial appearance, I will then move to the -- perhaps what is the most important formality of this procedure and namely to formally charge you. Mr. Borovcanin, I would like you to stand up, please. First matter that I would like to raise relates to legal representation, and this I am tasked to do by the Statute itself, apart from the Rules. I did hear Madam Colleen Rohan state earlier on that she has been appointed as duty counsel for the purpose of today's initial appearance, and I do thank you, madam, for having accepted this in the first place. So as far as today's representation is concerned, I would imagine that there is very little to say on your part. But if you have anything to say, please speak out now. For the time being, only as regards the representation during today's sitting by Ms. Rohan.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as for my legal representation, the duty counsel, I became acquainted with her yesterday and I realised that she was the duty counsel for this first initial appearance of mine. I have authorised her, I authorised her on time -- or rather, I have authorised Mr. Miodrag Stojanovic to represent me. I hope that I will receive a positive response because I think that electing him as counsel would be in the interests of justice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, I thank you. That is something that -- obviously it's very important for me as Pre-Trial Judge to know. That's something that I absolutely cannot comment upon today because it falls within the jurisdiction of the Registrar, who has to follow certain rules before he can proceed to assigning you proper counsel. And if Mr. Stojanovic qualifies, then I would imagine that there shouldn't be any problems. But I want you to understand that I am not in a position to comment any -- any further. I will later on come again on matters related to representation, but for the time being I can leave it at that because I am more interested for the time being as regards today's initial appearance. Now, Mr. Borovcanin, could you please give me your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Ljubomir Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. You're free to answer -- not to answer this question because it may provide an answer that could be later on useful to the Prosecution in matters of identification, but do you have a nickname?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do. My nickname is Ljubisa. Mostly people call me Ljubisa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you. Could I have your date of birth, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was born on the 27th of February, 1960.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And your place of birth, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Han Pijesak, Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And could you tell us what your nationality is at present.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm a Serb by nationality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Right. Now I will be asking you for your address, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. your last address, but I don't think that this is important for the public to know, so we'll go into private session for a while and then you can give me your last address. Let's go into private session, please. And don't answer before I tell you to do so.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, we are in open session now. I want to make sure that the members of your family are fully aware that you are present here in The Hague and that you are being detained in our Detention Unit in Scheveningen.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, they are fully aware of that, the members of my immediate family.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is there any member of your family, immediate and not immediate, that you would like me to inform as regards your transfer here and your state of detention here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, thank you. All those who need to know do know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Are the -- is your embassy aware that you are here in The Hague and in a state of detention?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I arrived under the organisation of the government of the Republic of Serbia and Montenegro. It was their organisation. They saw me off at the airport. There was two ministers escorting me in the airplane and tomorrow -- yesterday the representative of the government of Serbia and Montenegro visited me in the detention centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you need me to contact any member, any person from your embassy now, or even later, please do not hesitate to let me know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Borovcanin, I am soon going to ask you to sit down, but before I do so, I would like to inform you that before our Tribunal every accused, and that also includes you, of course, from the moment you are taken into custody until the very last second of the proceedings, whenever those will come to an end, you enjoy a number of rights. Some of them are substantial rights, some of them are procedural rights. Our Statute, which was approved by the Security Council of the United Nations spells out these rights, mainly in two articles, Articles 20 and Article 21. And I am now going to ask Madam Registrar to read out to you, and you will receive interpretation in the meantime, in their entirety these two articles. And then I will ask you whether you are fully aware of the import of these rights. You my sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You want me to state my views now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, no. Just sit down and these two Articles are going to be read out to you. Madam Registrar, could you please read out.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Article 20: "Commencement and conduct of trial proceedings. "1. The Trial Chamber shall ensure that a trial is fair and expeditious and that the proceedings are conducted in accordance with the Rules of Procedure and Evidence with full respect for the rights of the accused and due regard for the protection of victims and witnesses. "2. A person against whom an indictment has been confirmed shall, pursuant to an order or an arrest warrant of the International Tribunal be taken custody and be informed of the charges against him and transferred to an international Tribunal. "3. The Trial Chamber shall read the indictment, satisfy himself that the rights of the accused are respected, confirm that the accused understands the indictment and instruct the accused to enter a plea. The Trial Chamber shall then set the date for trial. "4. The hearing shall be public unless the Trial Chamber decides to close the proceedings in accordance with its Rules of Procedure and Evidence." Article 21: "Rights of the accused. "1. All persons shall be equal before the International Tribunal. "2. In the determination of charges against him, the accused shall be entitled to a fair and public hearing subject to Article 22 of the Statute. "3. The accused shall be presumed innocent until proven guilty according to the provision of the present Statute. "4. In the determination of any charge against the accused pursuant to the present Statute, the accused shall be entitled to the following minimum guarantees in full equality: (a) to be informed promptly and in detail in a language which he understands of the nature and cause of the charge against him; (b) to have adequate time and facilities for the preparation of his defence and to communicate with counsel of his own choosing; (c) to be tried without undue delay; (d) to be tried in his presence and to defend himself in person or legal assistance of his own choosing; to be informed, if he does not of legal assistance of this right; and to have legal assistance assigned to him, in any case where the interests of justice are so required, and without payment of him in any such case if he doesn't have means to pay for it; (e) to have examined, or have examined, the witnesses against him and to attendance and examination of witnesses on his behalf under the same conditions as witnesses against him; (f) to have the free assistance of an interpreter if he cannot understand or speak the language used in International Tribunal; (g) not to be compelled to testify against himself or to confess guilt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you -- I thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Borovcanin, could you please stand up again. You have heard Madam Registrar read out to you these two Articles which contain, as I explained earlier, your rights before this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have heard them, and I have understood them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Were you aware of their existence before coming here?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Someone has, I take it, explained the import of these rights?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have been following several trials going on here on television, and that was one of the information -- pieces of information that I heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Borovcanin, have you been served with a copy of the indictment in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have you read it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have you understood it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In other words, I take it that you are fully aware of the extent -- of the nature and extent of the charges that it contains in the six counts?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, you -- as I explained earlier, you have a right to have the indictment read out in full here, but you also have a right, should you so wish, to waive that right. And in that case, the summary that I provided earlier on would suffice even though in reality it is not even required by law. But for the time being, it would suffice. So before I proceed any further, Mr. Borovcanin, would you like us to read out the indictment in full or are you waiving this right?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am waiving the right to having the indictment read out in full.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. And the next step basically is the most important part of today's proceedings. I will be asking you to enter a plea to each and every one of the six counts that are contained in the indictment. There are these options: You can decide and you can enter a plea on these counts today. And your plea can be one either of guilty or of not guilty. You can ask to defer till later your entering such a plea, in which case I can only give you 30 days. If, either today or later on, but particularly later on within and until these 30 days, you decide to remain silent, in other words not to enter a plea at all, then I will enter a plea on your behalf, and that plea will be one of not guilty. Have you understood the three options?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused please be asked to speak into the microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have understood the options.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I have request from the interpreters to ask you to raise your voice a little and try and speak into the microphone as best you can. Are you prepared to enter a plea to the charges that are contained in the six counts of the indictment today or would you like to defer entering such a plea until later?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have understood the indictment. However, as the status of my Defence counsel who I have put forward has still not been settled, I would like to defer entering a plea and not enter a plea today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. You have every right to do that and I am making it clear once more that you have 30 days maximum within which to do that. For that purpose, either I, myself, or another Judge from my Trial Chamber - that's Trial Chamber II - will hold -- will preside over an additional initial appearance, or a continuation of today's initial appearance. And unless you give us to understand that you are and you wish to enter the plea earlier, that additional initial appearance will be held probably the last day of this 30-day period. The counts that you are charged with basically I made a reference to before, but for the benefit of the public I will just give just a little bit more detail. The first count is a charge of complicity in genocide, as I explained earlier, which is punishable under Article 4(3)(e) of the Statute of this Tribunal, and for this crime you are charged both with individual criminal responsibility pursuant to Article 7(1) and superior criminal responsibility under Article 7(3) of the Statute. The second count relates to a charge of extermination, which is a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5 of our Statute. Even here there is this dual criminal responsibility that is being attributed to you, that is responsibility under both subsection (1) and subsection (3) of Article 7. The third count contains a charge of murder, this being a crime against humanity, which is punishable as well under Article 5(A) of the Statute of this Tribunal, and even here the criminal responsibility that is being attributed to you in terms of the indictment is based both under section -- subsection (1) and subsection (3) of Article 7. The fourth count is also a charge of murder, but this times it's being imputed to you as a violation of the laws and customs of war, which is also punishable under Article 3 of our Statute. Again, Article 7(1) and 7(3) are being invoked as far as criminal responsibility is concerned. The fifth count is one of persecution, this being a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(H) of the Statute of this Tribunal, and again both subsections (1) and (3) of Article 7 of this Statute are being invoked against you. And finally, the sixth count contains a charge of inhumane acts consisting in forcible transfer, this being a crime against humanity punishable under Article 5(i) of the Statute of this Tribunal, and again Article 7(1) and Article 7(3) are being invoked. You may sit down. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There are a few final things that I need to state. First of all, Mr. Borovcanin, I would like to draw your attention to Rule 63 of our Rules of Procedure and Evidence, and particularly to the first paragraph of this rule. This rule lays down that questioning by the Prosecutor - and when I say "the Prosecutor" I don't mean just Madam Carla del Ponte and no one else, it could be any member of her office - questioning by the Prosecutor of an accused, including after the initial appearance, shall not proceed without the presence of counsel unless the accused has voluntarily and expressly agreed to proceed without counsel present. If the accused subsequently expresses a desire to have counsel, questioning shall thereupon cease and shall only resume when the accused's counsel is present. It's also important for you to note what is contained in the second paragraph of this Rule 63, namely, that the questioning, including any waiver of the right to counsel that you may make, shall be audio recorded or video recorded in accordance with the procedure which is provided in another rule, which is Rule 43 and which I don't need to read out to you, and the Prosecutor shall, at the beginning of the questioning, caution the accused in accordance with Rule 42(A)(iii). Rule 42(A)(iii) is an important rule that we have, and that is the Prosecutor, if at any time you are questioned, interrogated, have a duty to caution you as to the right -- your right to remain silent and that any statement or anything that you may say will be recorded and may be used in evidence. After this initial appearance - when I say "after" I don't mean necessarily today but within the next few days - I as Presiding Judge of Trial Chamber II will appoint a Pre-Trial Judge, who will first and foremost schedule a Status Conference which will be held within 120 days of the end of the initial appearance. This will be done in accordance or pursuant to Rule 65 bis (A) of the Rules. This will only be the first of several Status Conferences to follow if you plead not guilty. And Status Conferences are -- have two purposes: First of all, they are held in order to organise exchanges between the parties, Prosecution and Defence, on various matters such as, for example, disclosure of documents and preparation for the trial itself; and also to facilitate the expeditious preparation -- an expeditious preparation for trial. In addition - and perhaps this is something that must not at all costs be underestimated - it will give the Pre-Trial Judge and yourself an opportunity to see each other in person. And the Pre-Trial Judge will ensure that you are being treated well in the Detention Unit and would be ready to listen to any complaints or requests that you may have. This is why we hold Status Conferences periodically. When I say "periodically," by regulation Status Conferences are held not later than 120 days from each other. I signed an order on the 1st of April committing you to custody, where you will remain for the time being, but you may, in terms of Rule 65 of our Rules of Procedure and Evidence, file an application for provisional release. Filing an application for provisional release does Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. not mean that you automatically will be granted provisional release and it is very unlikely that provisional release be granted in the beginning or in the early stages of the proceedings. However, if you so choose, you so want, you can file an application for provisional release any time. Also, you can file it personally, if necessary, if you so want, pending the assignment of counsel. In other words, the fact that you may not have counsel assigned to you between now and I don't know when shall not be an impediment for -- for the purposes of filing an application for provisional release if you come to that -- the conclusion that you ought to file one. Of course, if you have counsel assigned to you, then that counsel will be in a position to assist you -- assist you in this. Mr. McCloskey, I am going to repeat what I repeat in every initial appearance, and it's something that I am hundred per cent sure that you are fully aware of. But I'm just reminding you that pursuant to Rule 66(A)(i) of the Rules, you need to make available to Defence counsel in a language which the accused understands all the supporting material which accompanied the indictment when confirmation was sought, and this needs to be done in 30 days of the initial appearance of the accused. Obviously the initial appearance does not end today. There is going to be an additional initial appearance, and the 30 days will start running from then. On your part, Mr. Borovcanin, I wish to draw your attention to Rule 72(A) of our Rules of Procedure and Evidence, which lays down or establishes a period of 30 days within which you are to file, if any, if at all, any preliminary motions that you might have and which that particular Rule deals with, 30 days once from when you have received the supporting material in accordance with Rule 66 that I mentioned earlier. Again, this is not something that you need to worry about today or tomorrow because there will be sometime before the documents which the Prosecution needs to disclose to your Defence counsel are disclosed. Obviously, if there is a delay in the assignment of counsel, Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Borovcanin, there is -- you can take my word for it that there will be an automatic delay in the 30-delay period that applies to you and subsequently to him. I don't believe there's anything much more for me to say. I address you, Mr. McCloskey, is there anything that you would like to raise at this point?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Borovcanin and Madam Rohan, both of you, is there any matter that either of you would like to raise at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MS. ROHAN
utterances.text: No. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And while you are standing up, please, I have a final question to you. I want to make sure because that is my duty, I want to make sure that from the moment you have been taken into the custody of this Tribunal and during the transfer and following the transfer your being taken into custody and kept in detention at the Detention Unit, you have at all times been treated well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the entire transfer up to the present moment, including accommodation at the Detention Unit, has been highly professional and proper. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. That is important for me to establish. It is something that practically each and every person that has come here confirms with a sole exception. I don't think there is anything else for me to add today. There will be an additional initial appearance in due course and you will receive the proper notification later on. I thank you. The initial appearance stands adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.17 p.m.
